artists.biography: "Public Service Broadcasting"  are a London-based pseudonymous musical group consisting of J. Willgoose, Esq. on guitar, banjo, other stringed instruments, samplings and electronic musical instruments, Wrigglesworth on drums, piano and electronic musical instruments, and J F Abraham on flugelhorn, bass guitar, drums and assorted other instruments including a vibraslap. The band have toured internationally and in 2015 they were announced as nominees in the Vanguard breakthrough category of the fourth annual Progressive Music Awards, staged by Prog magazine, which they won.

perplexity.description:
Every Valley is the third studio album by British art rock band Public Service Broadcasting, released in July 2017 on PIAS Recordings. Following the conceptual approach of their previous work, the album presents a thematic exploration of the Welsh coal mining industry, chronicling its rise and decline while serving as an allegory for deindustrialized communities across the Western world. Recorded at the Ebbw Vale Institute in South Wales, the album combines archive recordings and interview snippets with instrumental post-rock arrangements, featuring more original vocal performances than the band's earlier releases, including the vocal debut of principal songwriter J Willgoose, Esq.

Musically, Every Valley distinguishes itself through its lush, symphonic approach to industrial history rather than adopting the harsh, mechanical sound typically associated with the subject matter. The album employs layered strings, subtle guitar work, and brush patterns alongside contemporary and historical speech samples from miners and figures like Richard Burton, creating an emotionally nuanced portrait of the mining communities. Standout tracks like "Progress," featuring vocals from Camera Obscura's Tracyanne Campbell, balance critical reflection with euphoric celebration, embodying the album's tension between acknowledging industrial decline and honoring the resilience of working communities.

The album achieved commercial success in the United Kingdom and received highly positive critical reception. Critics praised its ability to convey human dignity and community spirit while maintaining a balanced, historically informed perspective on a pivotal period in British industrial history. The record was released across multiple formats including CD, digital download, vinyl, and a limited-edition clear vinyl variant.
